comparison: Both evaluate claims about NPRL2's antitumor efficacy in humanized vs non-humanized mice (C3-C5, C53-C56). OpenEval finds the data well-supported with appropriate statistics. Peer reviewers explicitly affirmed these findings as 'convincing in vivo data' without raising concerns.

Both address lack of synergy between NPRL2 and pembrolizumab in A549 tumors (C6, C58). OpenEval finds this clearly demonstrated by the data. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, noting 'inconsistent effect' and requesting clarification on how synergy was defined, questioning whether similar tumor intensity indicates lack of synergy.

Both evaluate synergy claims in H1299 tumors (C7, C75-C76). OpenEval finds the combination effect well-supported with statistical significance. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about the inconsistency between lack of synergy in A549 and presence of synergy in H1299, requesting better definition of synergy.

Both address NPRL2 efficacy in LLC2 anti-PD1 resistant model (C8, C82-C85). OpenEval finds strong support with significant tumor reduction. Peer reviewers accepted these findings without concerns, consistent with the overall narrative of NPRL2 effectiveness in resistant models.

Both evaluate comprehensive immune profiling data (C9-C12, C60-C64, C72-C74). OpenEval finds the flow cytometry data well-supported with appropriate statistics. Peer reviewers affirmed these findings, noting the work 'uncovers the advantage of NPRL2 gene therapy' with mechanism focused on dendritic cells and CD8+ T cells.

Both address functional T cell subset increases (C65-C69). OpenEval finds significant increases well-supported by flow cytometry. Peer reviewers accepted the immune profiling data without critique as part of the overall mechanism.

Both evaluate immune cell depletion experiments (C13-C16, C93-C97). OpenEval finds the mechanistic study clearly identifies cellular requirements for NPRL2 efficacy. Peer reviewers explicitly noted acceptance, stating 'the mechanism of NPRL2 gene therapy has focused on dendritic cells and CD8+T cells' via depletion studies.

Both address gene expression changes (C17-C23, C100-C101). OpenEval finds NanoString data appropriately analyzed and consistent with immune phenotypes. Peer reviewers did not question the gene expression data, accepting it as supporting the overall mechanism.

Both evaluate checkpoint molecule downregulation (C24, C102). OpenEval finds this supported by NanoString data and mechanistically relevant. Peer reviewers accepted the gene expression findings without critique.

Both address gene expression changes related to dendritic cells and macrophages (C103-C104). OpenEval finds consistency with flow cytometry data. Peer reviewers accepted these findings as part of the overall gene expression analysis.

Both evaluate bioinformatics analysis (C98-C99, C105-C107). OpenEval finds comprehensive pathway/network analyses appropriately conducted. Peer reviewers did not question these analyses, accepting them as supporting the mechanism.

Both address stable expression model validation (C25, C108-C116). OpenEval finds tumor growth and flow cytometry data validate transient transfection results. Peer reviewers accepted this data without critique as part of 'convincing in vivo data.'

Both evaluate synergy with chemotherapy (C26-C27, C117-C121). OpenEval finds colony formation, apoptosis, and Western blot data demonstrate synergy with clinical implications. Peer reviewers did not raise concerns about these in vitro findings.

Both address mTOR pathway inhibition (C28-C29, C122-C124). OpenEval finds Western blot data consistent with prior literature on NPRL2's role in mTOR regulation. Peer reviewers raised major concern about 'lack of systematic, and logical rigor,' questioning whether PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling is related to antigen presenting, the major mechanism of NPRL2's antitumor response.

Both evaluate cell cycle and apoptosis effects (C2, C49-C50, C125-C126). OpenEval finds cell cycle data supported and consistent with prior literature. Peer reviewers note uncertainty about relevance, stating 'This work did not present a link between apoptosis and antigen presenting induced by NPRL2 restoration.'

Both address differential PD-L1 response (C45-C46). OpenEval finds this clearly shown in Western blot data. Peer reviewers accepted the PD-L1 data itself but asked whether NPRL2 influences STING and LKB1, suggesting interest in upstream mechanisms.

Both evaluate integrative mechanistic conclusions (C30, C132, C138). OpenEval finds the dual mechanism (direct tumor effects and immune modulation) well-supported by converging evidence. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about logical integration, stating the work 'did not present a link between apoptosis and antigen presenting' and that 'the two parts may not support each other logically.'

Both address NPRL2 as tumor suppressor background (C1, C31-C32). OpenEval finds these well-supported by citations as established knowledge. Peer reviewers accepted these foundational background claims without question.

Both address prior work on NPRL2's cellular effects (C2, C33-C36). OpenEval finds these supported by citations as established background. Peer reviewers accepted these background claims without critique.

Both address clinical context of ICB resistance (C37-C40). OpenEval finds these supported by relevant literature citations. Peer reviewers accepted these as established background providing study rationale.
Both address background on related tumor suppressor (C41-C42). OpenEval finds these supported by citations establishing precedent. Peer reviewers accepted this background without question.
Both address complementary evidence from prior work (C128). OpenEval finds this supported by citation to Wang et al., 2022. Peer reviewers accepted this as background context.

Both address mechanistic background on mTOR regulation (C133-C137). OpenEval finds these supported by literature citations providing context. Peer reviewers accepted this background, though R10 questions the logical connection to immune effects.

OpenEval evaluates comparative efficacy in humanized vs non-humanized mice (C5). Peer R1 addresses broader efficacy claims including C5. Both find this comparison statistically significant and important for establishing immune involvement.

OpenEval evaluates differential PD-1 expression effects (C70-C71), finding distinct mechanisms between NPRL2 and pembrolizumab. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these claims.

OpenEval evaluates context-dependent immune effects in anti-PD1 sensitive tumors (C77-C81), finding appropriate statistical support. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these claims.

OpenEval evaluates comprehensive immune profiling in LLC2 syngeneic model (C86-C92), finding validation of immunomodulatory effects. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these claims.
OpenEval evaluates humanized mouse model methodology (C51-C52), finding it supported by citation and validated. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses methodology claims.

OpenEval evaluates mechanistic interpretation of pembrolizumab ineffectiveness (C129-C130), finding logical inference from experimental data. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses this interpretation.

OpenEval evaluates inference about pembrolizumab's limited functional T cell activation (C131), finding it supported by functional subset analysis. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses this specific inference.

OpenEval evaluates inference about antigen presentation mechanism (C132), finding it supported by depletion experiments. Peer R12 partially addresses this as part of broader mechanistic conclusions but questions logical integration.
